source.display_title: 05/11/2026 - Shawn Panjwani x Farooq Bey  — Follow Up

prospect.name: Steven Silbert
prospect.location: Baltimore, Maryland, USA — originally from California
prospect.occupation: Software engineer, remote, recently started a new job. Previously US Army, enlisted at 30, discharged a couple of years ago.
prospect.family_status: Engaged to Hannah, who lives with him; finances only recently being combined. Hopes to start a family soon.
prospect.training_background: Fifteen to seventeen years of Primal/Paleo training and eating since reading the Primal Blueprint in 2009. Left basic training at 187 lb and left the army close to 230 lb; current weight not asked or stated, self-describes as 'still overweight'. Rehabilitated his back with Foundation Training after a $350 private physical therapist. Over the last year has built back progressively through calisthenics, then kettlebells, then barbells for the first time since the injury. Familiar with Pavel's Simple & Sinister. Runs an early eating window and a prolonged fast once or twice a month.
prospect.medical: Herniated disc in the lower back sustained during army service, which laid him up for over a year and a half. Reports it as resolved — 'I feel like I'm not broken anymore' — after Foundation Training and private physiotherapy, and he is currently training with kettlebells and barbells. Describes ongoing achiness and creaky air squats, which he attributes to bodyweight rather than the disc.

signals: Lost ground to a specific injury and a hard season — herniated disc in the army, 187 lb to 230 lb, 'because of my back injury and everything'
Wants a former self back and can date it precisely: last felt right in his body 'probably five years ago', and 'I know what my potential is. I'd like to reach that potential again'
Carries the regret openly — 'even when other things are going good, I'll be like, ah, I wish I was back where I used to be. It kind of bums me out a lot'
Not the medically_constrained case: he considers the disc healed, is already doing loaded work, and no clinician has ruled anything out

goals.text: Restore his bodyweight-to-strength ratio — has gained strength but also a lot of weight
Be able to drop into any activity on impulse again — stand-up paddle boarding, jiu-jitsu, judo, sports generally
Strong joints and connective tissue, not just strong muscles, so the herniated disc does not recur
Longevity — be 'happy and hale and able to run around the kids' with a family he hopes to start soon
Feel like himself again and comfortable in his own skin; body is a big part of his identity

One authoritative plan to follow so he stops second-guessing and can stop carrying it as a worry — 'that's one less thing I have to worry about and more brain power I can give to my family and my work'
Learn kettlebells properly from an expert with form feedback

pains.text: Information overload after 15+ years of self-directed research — 'I have a lot of information... I don't have the time to put all of those various resources together and put a plan together for myself'
Gained roughly 43 lb from the end of basic training to leaving the army, driven by the back injury
Feels achy and lacking resilience — 'I guess I feel strong, but I also feel achy... just air squats are creaky'
Avoids the activities he loves because he does not trust his body in sudden fast movements at his current weight
Questions and abandons plans he wrote himself — 'if it's a plan that I made myself, like, it's easy for me to question it'
Social and relationship eating derails him — 'it's easy to kind of be like, oh, let's go out together and eat so-and-so. And that turns from a day to a week'
Cannot calibrate food to training load — 'what level of exercise warrants what amount of food', 'how many carbs is too many carbs? How do I track?'
Weak at warm-ups and recovery by his own admission
Half a decade of not feeling right in his body, which he says bums him out and undercuts him even when other things go well

objections.raw_quote: Well, I just need to discuss with my fiance.
objections.rep_response: Ran the partner play thoroughly — established Hannah was in the house, got her name, checked she was supportive, told the Oklahoma story about a wife joining a call and signing up, invited her to join, asked whether they had made a decision at this level before and whose idea it was, then isolated the blocker to finances

objections.raw_quote: She's more stringent on the strings, on the first strings. So it's going to be a much longer conversation. Because the first two, it's like $100, $200. And then like close to $1,000, it's like, okay, it's going to be a much longer conversation.
objections.rep_response: Isolated with 'if you guys find a way to make the finances make sense, you're in?' and got a yes, then dropped straight to a $1,200 one-month 'Love It or Leave It' trial rather than running the financial picture

objections.raw_quote: No, I'm still going to have to talk with her, sorry.
objections.rep_response: Fell back to the scripted deposit move — booked a 15-minute follow-up for the next day and took a refundable deposit at an amount the prospect chose himself

offer.payment_plan_terms: No plan structured. A $1,200 one-month 'Love It or Leave It' entry was offered, described inconsistently as both a cancellable trial and as 'the minimum payment to get actually into the program'. A refundable deposit was then taken at an amount the prospect chose — $100 of an offered range of $100 to $600.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: On the $1,200 entry only: 'if she says, all right, like, I'm not a fan of this, we can just cancel the program after that first month.' On the deposit: 'it's refundable... if we're meeting up on the call, and you say, oh, Hannah said no way, we just give you the refund for the deposit.'

evidence: No verbal agreement to the programme. Asked directly 'Do you want to move forward with that?' he answered 'No, I'm still going to have to talk with her, sorry.'

A $100 refundable deposit WAS paid and confirmed on the call — 'Yep, it went through' / 'Yep, I've seen that' — via a PayFunnels link, but it buys a calendar slot, not the programme, and is explicitly refundable if Hannah says no
Follow-up booked for 5pm Central the next day; the rep described it as 'just like 15 minutes of us catching up'
Close rule deliberately NOT applied: a payment link was sent and money moved, but there was no verbal agreement to move forward — the two conditions are cumulative, and only one is met
Positive counter-evidence: strong stated intent throughout — 'I think this is what I needed, really' and 'if you guys find a way to make the finances make sense, you're in?' / 'Yeah.'
outcome.next_step: 15-minute follow-up call the next day at 5pm Central after he speaks to Hannah. Rep also offered to email him a game plan for that conversation.

notable.note: This file is mis-titled. It contains two minutes with Shawn Panjwani, who had only 15 minutes and rescheduled to the next day without any discovery taking place, followed by a complete and unrelated 39-minute sales call with Steven Silbert. Any analysis keyed on the title attributes this call to the wrong prospect and counts a call that never happened. On the call itself: the strongest discovery in this batch by some distance, and then three improvised commercial structures in the last eight minutes — a $1,200 'Love It or Leave It' month described contradictorily as both a cancellable trial and 'the minimum payment to get actually into the program', a deposit whose amount the buyer was invited to set ('you choose the amount, 500 bucks, 100 bucks, I literally don't care'), and an offer to email the prospect a script for the conversation with his fiancée. Also note this call continues in a separate file dated 05/12/2026.

quality.notes: Two distinct prospects appear under separate labels ('Shawn's iPhone' then 'Steven Silbert') in one file. Within the Steven portion the labels invert constantly — 'So I'll leave the floor over to yourself. How can we potentially help you?' and 'Why do you say fear?' are labelled Steven but are clearly the rep, while 'Because I know what good feels like and is' and 'It's a little paradox, isn't it?' are labelled Farooq but are the prospect. Role resolved from content only. The rep also mangles the fiancée's name three ways across the call — Hannah, Anna and Tana.
